messages:
alex: Heads-up — planning a terraform apply during Tue 02:05 UTC change window. Scope: subnet tagging + iam role split. Deploybot will run at 02:05.
maria: Can we pin the AWS provider and the modules? last time an unpinned provider caused drift in staging.
samir: Agree. I'll add provider = \"hashicorp/aws\" ~> 4.0 to root and update the lockfile. PR incoming.
chloe: We need explicit rollback criteria in the release notes. Suggested quick triggers: error rate >1.5% for 15m or p50 latency +3s across services.
alex: My minimal rollback checklist:
- deploybot apply errors -> auto-abort
- post-apply smoke tests fail -> immediate rollback
- any KMS/permission denials observed -> rollback
- >2% 5xx in infra metrics for 10m -> consider rollback
maria: Also propose staged rollout: canary apply to two non-prod accounts first, wait 30m, then full rollout. reduces blast radius.
samir: I'll coordinate canary runs. infra-oncall, you good to watch the canary window 02:05-03:00 UTC?
infra-oncall: Yep. I'll be on the dashboard and have escalation path ready. Set alerts at errors >1% or p50 latency +5s for immediate paging.
chloe: PR for release notes and rollback playbook merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/423 (contains runbook, smoke commands, and rollforward/rollback steps)
alex: Plan excerpt attached:
```
# aws_iam_role.service-role will be updated in-place
~ resource \"aws_iam_role\" \"service-role\" {
  name = \"service-role\"
  # (omitted)
}
```
maria: Also pin module source versions in registry.tf to avoid automatic upstream module bumps.
samir: PR link for provider pin + lockfile: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/424

deploybot: @here preflight checks started — terraform fmt OK, terraform validate OK, plan generated. Plan: 12 to update in-place, 0 deletes, 2 creates.
alex: We'll run deploybot apply for canary accounts first at 02:05 UTC. If smoke passes, proceed to remaining accounts at 02:40 UTC.
infra-oncall: Dashboard URL: https://dashboards.internal.redwood.io/d/infra/change-window-1752109876
infra-oncall: Smoke tests scripted steps: `./scripts/smoke-checks.sh` against service endpoints, then check logs for KMS errors.

deploybot: preflight complete. plan saved to /deploys/1752109876/plan.json
alex: Kicking canary apply now. I'll keep this thread pinned and update frequently. :thumbsup:

deploybot: starting apply (canary account) — step 1/4: applying IAM role changes
oncall-bot: smoke test (canary) started: 20 checks
oncall-bot: smoke test (canary) results: 20/20 passed

deploybot: canary apply completed: 2 created, 3 updated in-place. No errors.
alex: canary looks good. waiting 30m for stability window.

infra-oncall: monitoring: error rate steady, no KMS denies. p50 latency unchanged.

(30m pass)

alex: proceeding to full rollout at 02:40 UTC.
deploybot: starting apply (global) — step 1/4
deploybot: apply completed: 10 updated in-place, 0 deletes, 0 failed
oncall-bot: post-apply smoke: 60/60 passed
infra-oncall: metrics: 5xx at baseline, p50 +0.6s — within thresholds

chloe: Release notes updated with canary summary and rollout timestamp. :tada:
samir: leaving a follow-up ticket to rotate tags and update module versions in next minor window: https://go/redwood/ticket/INFRA-912
alex: Closing the window. If anyone sees regressions, reopen this thread and tag infra-oncall. Great work team.
chloe: Adding manual rollback steps to the playbook for quick reference:
1) revert infra repo to commit before merge
2) run `terraform apply -auto-approve` in target account with state lock
3) notify product/security and open incident if needed

maria: Thanks all. We'll keep the provider lock for the next three releases.

samir: I'll follow up with a tidy PR for module version pins.

deploybot: note: artifacts saved at /deploys/1752109876/artifacts.tar.gz
alex: done, moving to postmortem/checklist updates. :white_check_mark:
